medSchoolStudLife.diversity: At the Keck School of Medicine, the Office of Student Engagement and Cultural Affairs (OSECA) is committed to cultivating a campus environment that respects, embraces, and celebrates students of all backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. We aim to meaningfully reflect the communities where we live, work, and serve.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be arranged by the Associate Dean for Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: In addition to the unparalleled learning opportunities offered by the Keck School of Medicine of USC, students get the opportunity to participate in student led interest groups of the various medical specialties, national medical student organizations, and University sponsored extracurricular activities. Los Angeles is  a city rich in culture and history, and known as the entertainment capital of the world. The University ticket office offers many discounted tickets to a variety of entertainment and sporting events.  In addition, due to Los Angeles' proximity to mountains, deserts and ocean , students can take a break from their studies at the beach, or go hiking, cycling or skiing; all within a short distance from our campus.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located on USC's Health Sciences Campus, the 31-acre medical campus is part of a largely Spanish speaking community in northeast Los Angeles. The campus is a short drive away from many of the recreational, cultural, and entertainment activities that Los Angeles has to offer.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Currie Hall https://www.americancampus.com/student-apartments/ca/los-angeles/currie-hall  has become home to the majority of first year students since its opening in September 2016. Students also reside in other nearby Los Angeles neighborhoods such as Boyle Heights, Highland Park, Glassell Park, Echo Park, Silver Lake, Koreatown, Lincoln Heights, Chinatown, Little Tokyo, Downtown, Hollywood, Los Feliz. Some students live in neighboring cities like Alhambra, Monterey Park, San Gabriel, South Pasadena, Pasadena, Glendale, Culver City, and Santa Monica.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
Office of Student Accessibility Services (OSAS) - The Office of Student Accessibility Services (OSAS) is the unit at USC responsible for ensuring equal access for students with disabilities in compliance with state and federal law. OSAS serves undergraduate, graduate and professional students; on-ground and on-line students; and students in all credit-granting courses and programs of study. https://osas.usc.edu/

Learning Enhancement and Academic Support Office - The KSOM Learning Enhancement and Academic Development (LEAD) unit provides an array of services and resources to help medical students master the curriculum. https://keck.usc.edu/md-program/academic-support/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: At the Keck School of Medicine, we believe that part of your education is knowing how to find balance because you can only take care of others when you are at your best. Find out by clicking on the link below. https://keck.usc.edu/md-program/wellbeing/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: MD students at the Keck School of Medicine of the University of Southern California receive an education that uniquely emphasizes equity, compassion and service. Located in one of the world’s most diverse settings, students engage with patients from different backgrounds, participate in research that represents the broader population, and provide patients cutting edge care. There is no better place to develop the clinical skills and human compassion that will change medicine in the 21st century. The Keck School of Medicine of USC prides itself on providing its students, faculty and staff a stimulating, collaborative, and supportive environment that encourages all members of our community to thrive. Through mentorship and guidance, faculty inspire the next generation of medical leaders, fostering a culture of excellence and compassion within the school.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students are required to have transportation to clinical sites that may be 40 or more miles from the HSC Campus.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Keck Learning Enhancement and Academic Development provides students with advisement, workshops, peer tutoring and one on one support. Please see https://keck.usc.edu/md-program/academic-support/
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Beginning in the first few weeks of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clerkships begin after the 18 month pre-clerkship phase; second semester of year 2.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Most lectures have the option to webcast. A small proportion of lectures require attendance.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Physician-Citizen-Scholar MD Curriculum emphasizes active learning strategies, early clinical immersion, and a learning environment that fosters the wellbeing and professional development of students. It is anchored by longitudinal coursework and experiential learning in Health Justice. All KSOM students are trained in how social determinants of health affect the health outcomes of individuals and populations while ensuring that students acquire skills in community assessment, health policy, and advocacy that can be used to advance health equity. All KSOM students receive a Certificate in Health Justice to reflect the core nature of this comprehensive and immersive curriculum. Please see https://keck.usc.edu/md-program/curriculum/
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The Keck School of Medicine Primary Care Program is a curriculum set to train primary care focused medical students in community health settings. Students are chosen from an annual application process. They are provided with opportunities to build longitudinal relationships with patients and primary care faculty throughout their four years of medical school. Under the supervision of faculty mentors, students become a part of a community-based care team, and learn about continuity of care, the patient-center medical home, community medicine and primary care leadership.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The Keck School of Medicine is home to a vibrant scientific community where researchers and clinicians collaborate to create a continuous loop of care – truly embodying the bench to bedside ideal. The Keck School’s rigorous research portfolio spans basic, clinical, translational and population research and utilizes multi-disciplinary collaborations in order to provide solutions for the health problems facing local and international communities.  Medical students have the opportunity to participate in funded summer and year-long research programs, and research electives that meet graduation requirements.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Curriculum is delivered in three phases with longitudinal integration of content and experiences, including scientific and clinical foundations, clerkship and post-clerkship phases.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service learning is a curricular component   Also, a large percentage of student interest groups participate in community service activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A Scholarly Project may be bench or clinical research.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: In addition to its century old collaboration with Los Angeles General Hosp., the medical school has teaching affiliations with Children's Hospital of Los Angeles, Keck Hospital, Norris Cancer Center
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass/Fail in Pre-clerkship Phase
Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail in Required Clerkship Phase
Credit, No Credit in Post-Clerkship Electives and Selectives

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Keck School of Medicine of the University of Southern California was established in 1885 as the region's first medical school. All students train at the Los Angeles General Hospital, one of the largest medical teaching centers in the United States. Through affiliations with over a dozen other private and public hospitals, students receive a remarkably broad clinical training experience.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Our mission is to ignite discovery through education, research and patient care, optimizing health for individuals, our diverse communities and society as a whole.

medSchoolApplication.matricNote: Note: Matriculant total includes two MD/DDS.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
A committee letter (or letter packet) is sufficient and preferable. Submission of a letter generated by the university fulfills all of our requirements without regard to the composition of that letter. If a committee letter or letter packet is used by your institution, please do not send additional individual letters!

For the individual letter option, 2 or 3 individual letters from professors, PI's or work experience are acceptable. If choosing the individual letter option, DO NOT submit more than 3 individual letters!!

An exception is made for MD/PhD applicants who may submit up to 6 individual letters.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: The applicant may choose whomever they believe can best speak to their personal and academic strengths. Letters of evaluation from faculty who know you well are especially valuable to the committee. "Physician" letters are not needed.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Provided to applicants upon being invited to interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: All applicants selected for a virtual interview will participate in a welcome session, an interview with a faculty member, and an interview with a current student on the same day. Questions and answers sessions will also be provided to interviewees.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Live, virtual interviews will be conducted.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Only AMCAS-certified applicants whose MCAT score is 506 or above will be invited to complete our secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Please see the program's website at https://keck.usc.edu/education/md-program/admissions/

MCAT Tests – All applicants must complete the MCAT as part of the application process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Although a single strong MCAT score is always the best strategy, we consider all MCAT scores in making decisions regarding candidacy. A sequence of scores tells us about timing and judgment as well as mastery of the material. Scores are not the sole determinants of an applicant’s acceptability. They are considered in relation to all of the other components of an application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: In general, applicants with MCAT scores below 506 are not invited to complete our secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: GPA trends are as important as the scores themselves.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: No minimum undergraduate GPA required. We consider postbacc grades a reliable indicator of academic strength. However,  grades from graduate programs do not remediate a weak undergraduate performance. The exception to this would be a rigorous "Special" Master's Program designed for students interested in medical school.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: No minimum number of  credit hours required. We consider postbacc grades a reliable indicator of academic strength. However,  grades from graduate programs do not remediate a weak undergraduate performance. The exception to this would be a rigorous "Special" Master's Program designed for students interested in medical school.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: All completed coursework submitted as part of the AMCAS Primary Application will be included in the evaluation of the application. We do not require any specific coursework for application eligibility.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
The large size of our applicant pool prohibits our admissions committee from accepting updates, letters of interest, or any addenda to the submitted Primary and Secondary applications. 
Letters of Intent are accepted from waitlisted candidates beginning on the first day of PTE.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Please visit our website for a full description of our Technical Standards.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: A variety of university scholarships and loans are available to supplement federal and state programs.  Recruitment scholarships are awarded to exceptional students each year.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Designed for Career Changers
For over two decades, the University of Southern California’s Postbaccalaureate Premedical Program has been preparing compassionate, intelligent and dedicated students for the pursuit of medical doctoral degrees. Designed for students that have successfully completed an undergraduate degree in a non-science field, this career changer program enables students to excel in a competitive academic environment, collaborate with peers and encourage each others’ development through each stage of the premedical preparation process.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: AMCAS application deadline (If November 1st falls on a holiday or weekend, the deadline will be the following business day)
Keck School of Medicine of USC Supplemental application deadline
In the  AMCAS Choose Your Medical School (CYMS) Tool, the "Plan to Enroll"  option becomes available.
Applicants must "Plan to Enroll" on April 30, 2026 in the CYMS Tool. The "Commit to Enroll" option also becomes available.

"Commit to Enroll" option becomes available April 30, 2026 in CYMS Tool. The "Commit to Enroll" action may be entered from April 30- July 3rd. July 3rd, 2026 is the commit to enroll deadline. Applicants also submit decisions directly to the Admissions Office, and can contact the office with decision inquiries.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: On or after April 30, 2027, wait-listed applicants may inform the Admissions Office of their desire to attend by emailing a brief letter of intent to medadmit@usc.edu.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: We recognize that each applicant has a personal path to medicine that cannot and should not be completely standardized.  Thus, we do not have specific course requirements.  However, we do expect that an applicant has demonstrated a high degree of academic excellence in their chosen field of study and possess the qualities and skills needed for this career of service.  A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or University in the U.S., or its equivalent  must be conferred before matriculation. Applicants' international coursework must be equivalent to a U.S. baccalaureate degree. Applicants with international coursework who are  invited to interview, will be asked to submit their evaluated coursework at that time.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The Admissions Committee considers candidates whose academic achievement and MCAT performance indicate the ability to satisfactorily complete the rigorous demands of the medical school curriculum. The committee also evaluates various non-academic factors, including personal motivations, evidence of integrity and ethics, reliability and dependability, significant achievements in extracurricular pursuits, research, and/or a demonstrated commitment to service and citizenship.
Please note that an application will be reviewed when complete and a decision may be rendered even if other activities, letters or MCAT scores are planned.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Approximately forty hours of primary care shadowing is usually sufficient.
